output.summary: The PR changes inBounds from `index < length` to `index <= length`, which breaks the documented contract. For nonnegative integer length the valid indices are 0 through length-1, and empty collections have no valid index; the new comparison wrongly treats index == length as in bounds. Frozen CI counterexamples inBounds(3,3) and inBounds(0,0) now return true instead of false.

findings.title: Off-by-one bounds check accepts index == length
findings.body: src/bounds.ts now returns `index >= 0 && index <= length`. This makes an index equal to the collection length report as in bounds, although the public contract states valid integer indices are 0 through length-1 and empty collections (length 0) have no valid index. As a result inBounds(3,3) returns true (expected false) and inBounds(0,0) returns true (expected false), allowing an out-of-range access at the length position.
findings.evidence: Current source line 2: `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. Diff changed `index < length` to `index <= length`. Synthetic CI frozen counterexamples: {index:3,length:3} expected false observed true; {index:0,length:0} expected false observed true.
findings.suggestion: Restore the strict comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`

output.diagnosis: The bounds predicate was altered from strict less-than to less-than-or-equal, causing index == length to be classified as valid even though valid indices only range from 0 to length-1 and empty collections have no valid index.
